7e5ed817f32380ce.en_html: The first change was that I became clear about what I wanted to do. At an IDFC preparatory study session, I met a Myanmar person living in Japan who supported refugee camps in Myanmar. Through that connection, I visited a refugee camp myself. There I saw people who had been persecuted by the previous military regime. If the people I had met in Yangon through IDFC represented Myanmar’s visible face, I felt I had now seen its hidden side. I had already been interested in journalism, but this made me strongly want to report on both the visible and hidden sides of things. I put myself forward for the organizing committee and insisted on holding the conference in the regional city of Mandalay in the second year of IDFC. Behind that was my wish to show participants these less visible aspects of Myanmar and encourage them to think more deeply.
